\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{ब्याव} (byāv)}{ब्याव (byāv)}]{\mw{ब्याव} (byāv) — a wedding; a marriage}

\label{lesson:MW-C247-byav}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to pass (of time), then the Marwadi for to die.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{ब्याव}}
\textbf{\mw{ब्याव}} — \emph{byāv} — \textquotedblleft{}a wedding; a marriage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{आज} \mw{गांव} \mw{मांय} \mw{ब्याव} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āj gā̃v mā̃y byāv hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is a wedding in the village today.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{ब्याव}} (\emph{byāv}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{vivāha}, \textquotedblleft{}marriage\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{byāha} under it (CDIAL 11920).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{byāv}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{byāv}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āj gā̃v mā̃y byāv hai.} — There is a wedding in the village today.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to pass (of time), then the Marwadi for to die, then say \emph{byāv} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{ब्याव} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A wedding; a marriage\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{टीको} (ṭīko)}{टीको (ṭīko)}]{\mw{टीको} (ṭīko) — a mark on the forehead}

\label{lesson:MW-C247-tiko}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to die, then the Marwadi for a wedding.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{टीको}}
\textbf{\mw{टीको}} — \emph{ṭīko} — \textquotedblleft{}a mark on the forehead\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{म्हारो} \mw{टीको} \mw{लाल} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mhāro ṭīko lāl hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mark on my forehead is red.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{टीको}} (\emph{ṭīko}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*ṭikka}, \textquotedblleft{}mark, spot\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Marwari \emph{ṭīko}, a mark worn on the forehead, under it (CDIAL 5458).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭīko}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭīko}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mhāro ṭīko lāl hai.} — The mark on my forehead is red.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to die, then the Marwadi for a wedding, then say \emph{ṭīko} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{परणणो} (paraṇṇo)}{परणणो (paraṇṇo)}]{\mw{परणणो} (paraṇṇo) — to marry; to get married}

\label{lesson:MW-C247-paranno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a wedding, then the Marwadi for a mark on the forehead.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{परणणो}}
\textbf{\mw{परणणो}} — \emph{paraṇṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to marry; to get married\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{म्हारो} \mw{मामो} \mw{काल} \mw{परण्यो।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mhāro māmo kāl paraṇyo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle got married yesterday.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \mw{वो} \mw{सावण} \mw{मांय} \mw{परण्यो}, \emph{vo sāvaṇ mā̃y paraṇyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{परणणो}} (\emph{paraṇṇo}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{pariṇayati}, \textquotedblleft{}leads round\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}marries\textquotedblright{}, from the rounds of the wedding; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{paraṇaï}, \textquotedblleft{}marries\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 7819).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paraṇṇo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paraṇṇo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mhāro māmo kāl paraṇyo.} — My uncle got married yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for a wedding, then the Marwadi for a mark on the forehead, then say \emph{paraṇṇo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{परणणो} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To marry; to get married\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{लाडी} (lāḍī)}{लाडी (lāḍī)}]{\mw{लाडी} (lāḍī) — a bride}

\label{lesson:MW-C247-ladi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a mark on the forehead, then the Marwadi for to get married.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{लाडी}}
\textbf{\mw{लाडी}} — \emph{lāḍī} — \textquotedblleft{}a bride\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{लाडी} \mw{घणी} \mw{सुंदर} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lāḍī ghaṇī sundar hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bride is very beautiful.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{लाडी}} (\emph{lāḍī}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*lāḍya}, \textquotedblleft{}fondling\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{lāḍalī}, \textquotedblleft{}fondling\textquotedblright{}, and Gujarati and Sindhi \emph{lāḍī}, \textquotedblleft{}bride\textquotedblright{}, under it; the bride is probably named as the family's darling (CDIAL 11013).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lāḍī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lāḍī ghaṇī sundar hai.} — The bride is very beautiful.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for a mark on the forehead, then the Marwadi for to get married, then say \emph{lāḍī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{लाडी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A bride\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{मांडवो} (mā̃ḍvo)}{मांडवो (mā̃ḍvo)}]{\mw{मांडवो} (mā̃ḍvo) — a wedding pavilion}

\label{lesson:MW-C247-madvo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to get married, then the Marwadi for a bride.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{मांडवो}}
\textbf{\mw{मांडवो}} — \emph{mā̃ḍvo} — \textquotedblleft{}a wedding pavilion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{घर} \mw{कनै} \mw{मांडवो} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ghar kanai mā̃ḍvo hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is a wedding pavilion beside the house.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{मांडवो}} (\emph{mā̃ḍvo}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{maṇḍapa}, \textquotedblleft{}an open shed, a pavilion\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{maṇḍavo} and \emph{māḍhivo}, \textquotedblleft{}a pavilion\textquotedblright{}, and Gujarati \emph{mā̃ḍvo}, \textquotedblleft{}a booth\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 9740).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mā̃ḍvo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mā̃ḍvo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghar kanai mā̃ḍvo hai.} — There is a wedding pavilion beside the house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to get married, then the Marwadi for a bride, then say \emph{mā̃ḍvo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{मांडवो} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A wedding pavilion\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from A Fall in the Lane to A Wedding in the Village}

\label{lesson:MW-R247-review-241-247}



\begin{quote}
Say the Marwadi for an injury and a stumble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item an injury, a stumble, a wound, to get broken, to slip
  \item to get burnt, to go out (of a flame), to crack open, a potsherd, to sink
  \item a theft, to rob, to snatch away, to go missing, to cheat
  \item a quarrel, to fight, a lie, a fault, a threat
  \item to call someone over, a respectful greeting, to draw near, a surprise, congratulations
  \item a woman's parents' home, a woman's in-laws' home, an invitation, to pass (of time), to die
  \item a wedding, a mark on the forehead, to get married, a bride, a wedding pavilion
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An injury? (\textbf{\mw{चोट}}, \emph{choṭ}.) A stumble? (\textbf{\mw{ठोकर}}, \emph{ṭhokar}.) A wound? (\textbf{\mw{घाव}}, \emph{ghāv}.) To get broken? (\textbf{\mw{टूटणो}}, \emph{ṭūṭṇo}.) To slip? (\textbf{\mw{खिसकणो}}, \emph{khisakṇo}.) To get burnt? (\textbf{\mw{जळणो}}, \emph{jaḷṇo}.) To go out (of a flame)? (\textbf{\mw{बुझणो}}, \emph{bujhṇo}.) To crack open? (\textbf{\mw{फूटणो}}, \emph{phūṭṇo}.) A potsherd? (\textbf{\mw{ठीकरो}}, \emph{ṭhīkro}.) To sink? (\textbf{\mw{डूबणो}}, \emph{ḍūbṇo}.) A theft? (\textbf{\mw{चोरी}}, \emph{chorī}.) To rob? (\textbf{\mw{लूटणो}}, \emph{lūṭṇo}.) To snatch away? (\textbf{\mw{खोसणो}}, \emph{khosṇo}.) To go missing? (\textbf{\mw{गमणो}}, \emph{gamṇo}.) To cheat? (\textbf{\mw{ठगणो}}, \emph{ṭhagṇo}.) A quarrel? (\textbf{\mw{झगड़ो}}, \emph{jhagṛo}.) To fight? (\textbf{\mw{लड़णो}}, \emph{laṛṇo}.) A lie? (\textbf{\mw{झूठ}}, \emph{jhūṭh}.) A fault? (\textbf{\mw{दोस}}, \emph{dos}.) A threat? (\textbf{\mw{धमकी}}, \emph{dhamkī}.) To call someone over? (\textbf{\mw{तेड़णो}}, \emph{teṛṇo}.) A respectful greeting? (\textbf{\mw{जुहार}}, \emph{juhār}.) To draw near? (\textbf{\mw{ढूकणो}}, \emph{ḍhūkṇo}.) A surprise? (\textbf{\mw{अचंभो}}, \emph{achambho}.) Congratulations? (\textbf{\mw{बधाई}}, \emph{badhāī}.) A woman's parents' home? (\textbf{\mw{पीहर}}, \emph{pīhar}.) A woman's in-laws' home? (\textbf{\mw{सासरो}}, \emph{sāsro}.) An invitation? (\textbf{\mw{नूतो}}, \emph{nūto}.) To pass (of time)? (\textbf{\mw{बीतणो}}, \emph{bītṇo}.) To die? (\textbf{\mw{मरणो}}, \emph{marṇo}.) A wedding? (\textbf{\mw{ब्याव}}, \emph{byāv}.) A mark on the forehead? (\textbf{\mw{टीको}}, \emph{ṭīko}.) To get married? (\textbf{\mw{परणणो}}, \emph{paraṇṇo}.) A bride? (\textbf{\mw{लाडी}}, \emph{lāḍī}.) A wedding pavilion? (\textbf{\mw{मांडवो}}, \emph{mā̃ḍvo}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
